title: ProofChain: tamper-evident proofchain for dedicated capacity data boundaries and retention lifecycle
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a tamper-evident ProofChain service that produces cryptographically verifiable snapshots for dedicated capacity tenants describing: node geo-anchors, active retention policy applied to tenant data, retention lifecycle events (ingest, prune, export), and the exporter artifacts used for audits. The service should be usable by Redwood Private and Dedicated control planes and produce human-readable and machine-verifiable bundles for regulator/enterprise audits.
acceptance_criteria: ProofChain publishes an append-only daily snapshot containing tenant->node mapping, clocked timestamps, and retention policy hashes
Each snapshot is signed by HSM-backed signing key and includes a Merkle root for per-tenant evidence subtrees
Audit bundles (signed snapshot + per-tenant proofs + retention manifests) can be exported to S3/GCS or streamed to customer SFTP
Console shows last 30 days of ProofChain snapshots with verification status and links to exported bundles
Automated test harness verifies signature validity and detects any tamper by altering proof entries (CI regression)
tasks: Design on-disk format for per-tenant evidence subtree (Merkle-packed manifests)
Integrate with KMS/HSM for key rotation and signing APIs
Implement snapshot generator that queries dedicated orchestration (node assignments, zone metadata) and retention config service
Add exporter module to push bundles to configured sinks (S3/GCS/SFTP) with retry/backoff
Instrument Console with a ProofChain viewer and verification endpoint
Create CI tests: signing, verification, and synthetic tamper detection
decisions: Use Merkle-tree per snapshot to allow compact per-tenant proof verification (over full ledger)
Sign snapshots using HSM-backed key managed in KMS; ephemeral signing delegation tokens for worker processes
Store canonical snapshots in an append-only object store bucket with immutable object metadata and lifecycle rules
Export audit bundles as zipped signed artifacts plus an index.json containing the Merkle root and signatures
tradeoffs: Snapshot frequency vs. cost: daily snapshots chosen to balance operator cost and auditor expectations; can support ad-hoc snapshots for high-risk customers
On-disk Merkle representation increases snapshot generation CPU but reduces download size for per-tenant proofs
Strong HSM signing increases operational complexity but is required for enterprise attestation requirements
blockers: Awaiting KMS policy updates to grant signing rights to the ProofChain service (security ticket in progress)
Retention config API v2 (ENG-20133) needs small endpoint for export of canonical policy blobs
notes: Regulatory ask: EU customer compliance team requested daily signed residency evidence + 2-year retention of snapshots
We should coordinate with Solutions for packaging customer-facing attestation report templates
